papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models
papers.summary: Somnus is an open-source Python platform for automated sleep staging in rodents using EEG, EMG, and optional video. Its base model, trained across diverse recordings from six laboratories, enables rapid fine-tuning via a graphical interface that targets uncertain epochs, allowing accurate custom scorers for disease models with minimal manual correction.

papers.title: SSSI: A simulation-based framework for evaluating sigma-power fluctuation state identification pipelines in NREM sleep EEG.
papers.summary: The paper presents SSSI, a simulation-based framework that generates synthetic sigma-power fluctuations (SPFs) with known reference states to evaluate pipelines for identifying SPF states in NREM sleep EEG. Using a pipeline selected via SSSI, the authors found within-episode changes in SPF-state proportions in both mouse NREM and human N2 sleep, with age-dependent variation in humans, and demonstrated that detected effects can depend on the identification pipeline.

papers.title: Irreversible functional network deformation induced by preprocessing scheme order in multivariate EEG recordings.
papers.summary: The paper quantitatively compares two EEG preprocessing schemes that differ only in the order of filtering and re-referencing, using sleep EEG, synthetic models, and surrogate testing. It shows that re-referencing followed by filtering induces spurious cross-correlations that increase with frequency band and spectral exponent, becoming irreversible for steep spectra (β ≥ 2), whereas filtering followed by re-referencing introduces only small, correctable negative shifts; the authors recommend filtering followed by re-referencing with surrogate correction for such signals.

papers.title: NESTApp: A GUI-Based MATLAB Application for Auditable TMS-EEG Preprocessing with EEGLAB
papers.summary: The paper describes NESTApp, a GUI-based MATLAB application built on EEGLAB for constructing, applying, and automatically documenting customizable TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines with integrated quality control. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection, aiming to improve reproducibility and lower technical barriers in TMS-EEG preprocessing.

papers.title: What EEG doesn't see: a whole-brain MEG map of sleep spindles and slow oscillations
papers.summary: Simultaneous MEG/EEG during daytime naps in 19 young adults showed that sleep spindles and slow oscillations occur throughout the brain, including thalamus, hippocampus, and cerebellum, with region-specific balances between fast/slow spindles and SO frequency bands. A single scalp derivation (Cz-M1) provides a selective and partly composite view: more SOs were detected in every brain region than at Cz-M1, whereas fast spindles were more frequent at Cz-M1 than in any single source region.

papers.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: An automated interpretable pipeline using one hour of ICU cEEG estimated near-term seizure risk from interictal-ictal continuum probabilities and quantitative background features in 50 adults. For the 4-hour horizon, a combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy and Brier score 0.25, and accuracy declined from 94% at 1 hour to 79% at 24 hours, with initial external validation supporting generalizability.

papers.title: Visual cues in MI-BCI induce biases in EEG classification models with deep learning but not with standard machine learning.
papers.summary: This study evaluated whether including visual cue onset in EEG windows biases deep learning models for motor imagery BCI classification. It found that visual cue onset significantly improved accuracy for DeepConvNet and REVE, but attribution maps showed these models relied on cue-related visual evoked potentials rather than motor imagery sensorimotor rhythms (ERD/ERS), while CSP+LDA maintained consistent motor cortex activation and minimal accuracy change.

papers.title: Distinct electroencephalography alpha-band rhythms map macroscale brain gradients.
papers.summary: Using source-reconstructed resting-state EEG from 608 adults (3,255 recordings), the study found that 38.3% of recordings had separable alpha-frequency components that aligned with canonical functional networks, especially separating visual and somatomotor systems. Low-dimensional analysis identified a sensory-differentiation axis and a sensorimotor-association axis resembling functional-connectomic gradients, linking split alpha to macroscale cortical organization.

papers.title: Fixed-Sequence OFF-to-ON Differences in Low-Beta State Dynamics in Parkinson's Disease: A Paired Source-Space Resting-State EEG Study.
papers.summary: In 39 Parkinson's disease patients with paired OFF/ON resting-state EEG, low-beta (13-20 Hz) dynamic amplitude-envelope connectivity showed higher switching rate and entropy in the later ON session compared to the earlier OFF session, with lower fractional occupancy and mean dwell time of an OFF-dominant state. The fixed OFF-then-ON protocol confounds medication state with session order, time, vigilance, fatigue, and adaptation, so medication-specific effects cannot be distinguished.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic complexity and cognitive decline: Insights from approximate entropy across aging and dementia.
papers.summary: The paper examined EEG approximate entropy (ApEn) in 269 participants across healthy elderly, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's disease (AD) groups, finding progressive decreases in total ApEn from HE to MCI to AD, especially in central regions, with frequency-specific patterns and correlations with cognitive scores. A random forest classifier achieved 66.55% accuracy, with sensitivities of 78.90% (HE), 49.33% (MCI), and 65.88% (AD).

papers.title: An Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer for Participant-Level Classification of Depressive Symptoms From Resting-State EEG.
papers.journal: International journal of methods in psychiatric research
papers.summary: The paper develops an explainable self-supervised temporal transformer for participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG, using masked temporal pretraining and supervised fine-tuning. The model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73–0.90) and balanced accuracy of 0.75, with self-supervised pretraining improving performance over no pretraining (ROC-AUC 0.74), while explainability analyses identified temporally relevant intervals and frontal-midline to centro-parietal channel contributions; the authors caution that findings do not establish clinical diagnostic validity.

papers.title: Attenuated alpha state transitions and disrupted repetition-dependent temporal adaptation in mild cognitive impairment
papers.summary: In 77 participants with mild cognitive impairment and 60 healthy controls, occipital alpha (8-12 Hz) transitions during repeated eye-opening/eye-closure cycles were weaker and less successful in MCI, with no group difference in post-onset time constant. MCI showed absent repetition-dependent temporal adaptation: healthy controls developed later onset during eye opening and earlier onset during eye closure across trials, whereas MCI did not.

papers.title: Selective Auditory Attention Decoding with a Two-Node Wireless EEG Sensor Network
papers.summary: Evaluated selective auditory attention decoding using a two-node wireless around-ear EEG sensor network and achieved 69.24% accuracy on 60s windows, improving to 77.17% steady-state with HMM post-processing and 32.79s attention switch detection time.

papers.title: Robust and replicable effects of ageing on resting-state brain electrophysiology measured with MEG.
papers.summary: Using the GLM-Spectrum on eyes-closed resting-state MEG, this study estimates a full-frequency whole-head profile of ageing effects that replicates across open-access datasets and is robust to common covariates. Distinct frequency components have different effect sizes, and the age effect is partially robust to grey matter volume modeling, showing that targeting an age effect linearly separable from a covariate can reduce statistical power.

papers.title: An EEG-based framework for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis via single-channel multi-entropy fusion and ensemble learning.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine
papers.summary: Developed a single-channel EEG framework combining wavelet and empirical mode decomposition with multi-entropy features and ensemble learning, achieving 97.92% and 81.54% accuracy on two public datasets for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.

papers.title: MTDANet: lightweight multi-scale temporal hierarchy and distance-regularized linear attention network for motor imagery brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: Proposed MTDANet, a lightweight multi-scale temporal hierarchy and distance-regularized linear attention network for motor imagery EEG decoding, achieving 85.61%, 90.85%, and 87.79% subject-specific accuracies on three public datasets.

papers.title: AOR: adaptive orthogonal regression for depression feature selection with incomplete EEG channels.
papers.summary: Introduced adaptive orthogonal regression (AOR) for EEG feature selection under incomplete channel conditions, achieving average cross-subject depression recognition accuracies of 92.25% and 95.12% on MODMA and PRED-d003 datasets.

papers.title: Decoding object categories from electroencephalography during free viewing reveals early information evolution compared to passive viewing.
papers.summary: This study combined multivariate pattern analysis with deconvolution to decode object category information from EEG during free viewing and compared it to passive viewing. It found that category information could be decoded from individual fixations in free viewing, generalized across conditions, and emerged earlier when time-locked to fixation onset than to stimulus onset, suggesting parafoveal processing.

papers.title: Hypoxia Disrupts Multiple Processes Supporting Spatial Navigation
papers.summary: This study investigated whether continuous or intermittent hypoxia differentially affects spatial navigation and resting-state EEG in healthy young adults. Hypoxia impaired multiple navigation components, increasing path integration distance error and egocentric pointing angle error, while mapping accuracy was preferentially impaired after intermittent hypoxia and perspective taking after continuous hypoxia; hypoxia also reduced alpha and beta power, beta central frequency, and aperiodic exponent, with the aperiodic exponent reduction primarily after intermittent hypoxia, and SpO2 reduction did not predict individual differences.

papers.title: GROND: Automated characterization of periodic and rhythmic EEG patterns.
papers.summary: Presented GROND, an automated system for characterizing periodic discharges and rhythmic delta activity, achieving expert-level reliability in frequency, laterality, spatial localization, and discharge timing with ICC values exceeding expert-expert agreement.

papers.title: Long-term functional outcome after post-anoxic brain injury: model development and internal validation from a multicentre cohort.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In a multicentre cohort of 160 cardiac arrest patients, middle-latency somatosensory evoked potentials (ML-SSEPs) independently predicted good functional outcome at 12 months, while the interaction between continuous/nearly continuous EEG and N20/P25 predicted survival and recovery of consciousness. ML-SSEPs combined with EEG and standard SSEPs may improve ICU prognostication after post-anoxic coma.

papers.title: Acoustic Context Shapes Cortical Encoding of Spectral Discrimination in Normal and Impaired Hearing
papers.summary: This EEG study investigated how acoustic context and temporal-envelope variability shape cortical encoding of spectral contrast in normal-hearing and hearing-impaired listeners. The auditory change complex was larger and more symmetrical for discrete spectro-temporal modulations than conventional ones, decreased with spectral contrast, and was weaker and delayed in hearing-impaired listeners, while auditory steady-state responses remained contrast-insensitive.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in schizophrenia: enhancing transparency in clinical decision-making.
papers.summary: This review discusses how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) can improve transparency and clinical trust in machine learning models for schizophrenia, which often use multimodal neuroimaging and clinical data to predict diagnosis, treatment response, and relapse risk. It argues that XAI-integrated models can support biomarker discovery and personalized psychiatry while maintaining ethical and regulatory standards.

papers.title: How aging reshapes implicit learning: behavioral and oscillatory evidence from an EEG-adapted Fast Mapping paradigm.
papers.summary: Used an EEG-adapted Fast Mapping paradigm (DIILT) in 31 younger and 35 older adults to test age-related changes in implicit learning, with a one-month delayed recognition measure. Younger adults rapidly acquired novel implicit associations and showed early posterior theta engagement for novel items, while older adults showed limited novel-item improvement and no such theta modulation; implicitly learned associations were retained after one month more stably than explicitly encoded ones in both groups.

papers.title: Chronic Electrophysiology Captures Progressive Variability in DNA-Damaged Cardiac Networks
papers.summary: Using a microelectrode array system, this study chronically recorded electrophysiological activity from human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte monolayers for up to 40 days, capturing progressive declines in field potential amplitude, conduction velocity, and increased beat-to-beat variability after doxorubicin exposure. Electrode-resolved analyses revealed spatial variability in cardiotoxic responses that would be masked by population averages, and endpoint assays confirmed reduced calcium transients, mitochondrial membrane potential, and connexin 43 loss.

papers.title: Motor effort biases perceptual decisions through later-stage evidence accumulation rather than early sensory-attentional processing
papers.summary: Recorded 64-channel EEG in 24 healthy adults performing an orientation discrimination task with two pressure-sensitive response buttons requiring different force levels to determine when motor effort biases perceptual decisions. Motor effort reduced pre-stimulus alpha power contralateral to the low-effort option and increased pre-response centro-parietal positivity for low-effort choices without altering early P1/N1 sensory responses, with trial-by-trial CPP amplitude predicting low-effort selection, indicating a later-stage evidence accumulation bias.

papers.title: How do Uncompensated Micro-Shifts Systematically Confound Low-Concentration Metabolite Quantification in 1H-MRS Analysis?
papers.summary: Systematically evaluated how uncompensated frequency perturbations affect 1H-MRS linear combination model fitting using simulations and a public in vivo human brain dataset (n = 31). High-concentration metabolites showed minimal quantification changes, but low-concentration metabolites including Gln, GSH, Asp, and NAAG showed relative changes exceeding 10%-20%, often with CRLB values still within conventionally acceptable ranges, indicating that CRLB alone is insufficient for assessing quantification reliability.

papers.title: Toddler EEG power reflects behavioral social engagement state during naturalistic parent-child interaction.
papers.summary: This study recorded EEG from typically developing toddlers and an independent sample including children with autism during naturalistic parent-child interaction, finding that child EEG alpha power decreased and theta power increased during moments of social engagement relative to baseline movie watching. The pattern replicated across a range of social and linguistic abilities, linking EEG power to naturally occurring social engagement states.

papers.title: Large-scale all-optical electrophysiology links excitability and connectivity to circuit dynamics in vivo
papers.summary: Developed large-scale all-optical electrophysiology tools and applied them to approximately 300 layer 1 interneurons per mouse in vivo, identifying 1,469 inhibitory and 5,752 directed electrical connections among 14,312 tested pairs across two mice. Presynaptic identity was more strongly associated with IPSP amplitude and postsynaptic identity with IPSP decay time, and excitability under optogenetic stimulus predicted spontaneous spiking responses, linking cellular properties and pairwise interactions to circuit dynamics.

papers.title: Electrophysiological signature of stroke recovery: investigating EEG biomarkers for prognostic insights.
papers.summary: In stroke patients, resting-state EEG at 1 week and 3 months post-stroke showed that change in relative alpha power was the strongest single correlate of motor improvement (ΔFM). A hierarchical model combining alpha power, metastability/synchrony, and microstates explained over 78% of variance in motor recovery, suggesting that balanced alpha oscillations and flexible network coordination index recovery.

papers.title: Neurite Complexity and Plasticity Markers Track Synaptic Vesicle Density in the Living Human Brain: A Multimodal PET-MRI-EEG Study
papers.summary: Combined [11C]-UCBJ PET, DWI/NODDI, rs-fMRI, and EEG in 18 healthy volunteers to test relationships between synaptic SV2A density and structural/functional plasticity markers, with ketamine (n=11) or DMT (n=7) challenge. BPND was coupled with neurite orientation dispersion across cortical regions and associated with EEG measures of short-term and long-term synaptic plasticity, while no consistent association was found with rs-fMRI functional weighted degree.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Pain Threshold Index-Guided Remifentanil Titration During Laparoscopic Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized trial tested whether remifentanil titration guided by the EEG-derived pain threshold index reduces intraoperative remifentanil infusion during laparoscopic abdominal surgery. It found no significant difference in the primary endpoint: mean remifentanil infusion rate was 7.44 vs 7.63 µg kg-1 h-1 (adjusted difference -0.06; P=0.758). Exploratory secondary analyses showed lower PACU rescue opioid use and fewer PONV events with PTi guidance, but no reduction in total postoperative opioid exposure.

papers.title: Cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation in pediatric epileptic syndromes: mechanisms, limitations, and future research horizons.
papers.summary: This review evaluates cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation (c-tDCS) for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy, citing meta-analytic evidence of roughly 45% seizure-frequency reduction at 4 weeks and favorable tolerability across over 600 pediatric sessions. It highlights substantial inter-individual variability, inconsistent links between interictal discharge suppression and clinical outcomes, higher modeled cortical electric fields in children, and the need for biomarker-driven selection and adequately powered trials in specific developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

papers.title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Characteristics of Peripheral Neuropathy in Immune-Related Adverse Event of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Retrospective Study and Literature Review.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed 8 local cases and 42 published cases of peripheral neuropathy immune-related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitors, summarizing clinical, electrophysiological, treatment, and outcome data. Most patients presented with demyelinating sensorimotor involvement of upper and lower limbs, supporting early electromyography after neuropathic symptom onset.

papers.title: Attenuated attention engagement and sensorimotor resonance to social events in first-episode adolescent depression: Evidence from EEG oscillations.
papers.summary: Used EEG to measure sensorimotor mu suppression and occipital alpha activity during observation of social and non-social events in 22 adolescents with first-episode major depressive disorder and 23 healthy controls. Depressed adolescents showed no differential mu suppression for social versus control events and higher occipital alpha power to social targets, with attenuated sensorimotor resonance correlating with depressive symptom severity.

papers.title: Sustained Seizure Freedom After Stereo-Electroencephalography Without Definitive Intervention: Evidence for Network Modulation by Invasive EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Reported two patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who achieved sustained seizure freedom after stereo-EEG monitoring without resection, ablation, or neuromodulation. The findings suggest that sEEG implantation may have microlesional or network-modulatory effects, and that extended follow-up may be warranted when habitual seizures are not captured and early improvement occurs.

papers.title: Stress recovery and restorative effects of viewing different types of peony garden landscapes: a preliminary experiment.
papers.summary: Preliminary VR experiment with 56 participants per group compared stress recovery after viewing flatland, terraced, or mountainous peony gardens versus an indoor environment using TSST, physiological measures (HR, HRV, EEG), and psychological scales. Peony garden scenes improved physiological and emotional recovery relative to the indoor scene, with the most pronounced changes after the mountainous peony garden.

papers.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI
papers.summary: In a mouse controlled cortical impact model of TBI, daily post-injury treatment with the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100635 for 6 weeks preserved retinal ganglion cell survival and visual function, reduced microglial/macrophage activation and reactive astrogliosis, and improved motor and behavioral outcomes. Treatment did not significantly reduce cortical cavity volume, indicating preferential protection of perilesional and connected circuitry.

papers.title: Optimal Sound-Color Matching Scheme of Five-Element Music and Lighting Colors for Emotional Responses in Patients with GAD: A Randomized, Two-Factor Mixed-Design Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized two-factor mixed-design trial tested sound-color matching in 210 GAD patients and found that positive Five-Element music with cyan lighting produced the highest valence scores (7.79±0.81) and optimal physiological regulation (lowest HR reduction of -15.44±1.89 bpm; highest skin temperature increase of 0.84±0.09°C), with significant interactions for valence, arousal, skin temperature, heart rate, and EEG theta power.

papers.title: A Pilot Study of Photon Counting CT Spectral Analysis Following Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Resection to Differentiate Local Recurrence From Postsurgical Fibrosis.
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed photon counting CT spectral parameters in 22 post-pancreatic adenocarcinoma resection patients and found excellent differentiation of local recurrence from postsurgical fibrosis, with extracellular volume and normalized iodine density both achieving 100% sensitivity and specificity and near-perfect inter-reader agreement.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
